mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the access-control fact lets the model invent a successful operation by a caller whose role does not grant the operation. The injection forces a Customer to successfully invoke OpDecide, which the permission matrix denies, so both LeastPrivilege and FR-015 must surface a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilege { some op: Operation, u: User | op.invoker = u and u.role = CustomerRole and op.kind = OpDecide and op.outcome = OutAllow }

mutation_targets.rationale: Without the audit-events-exist fact, an application can reach Approved status without a corresponding EvApproved entry. The injection forces such a state, so audit-completeness assertions must fail.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompleteness { some a: LoanApplication | a.status = StApproved and (no e: ApplicationEvent | e.application = a and e.eventType = EvApproved) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the append-only fact removes the uniqueness constraint on (application, eventType). The injection forces two distinct audit events with the same application and eventType, which is exactly what AppendOnly forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnly { some disj e1, e2: ApplicationEvent | e1.application = e2.application and e1.eventType = e2.eventType }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the single-pending-per-customer fact allows the partial unique index's invariant to be violated. The injection forces two distinct Pending Review applications for the same customer.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OnePending { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.customer = a2.customer and a1.status = StPending and a2.status = StPending }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the ownership-check fact lets a customer's GetApp succeed against an application they do not own. The injection forces this exact instance. F_NoLeakOnNonOwnedRead does not block it because that fact's antecedent excludes outcome=OutAllow.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipBased { some op: Operation, c: User, a: LoanApplication | op.invoker = c and c.role = CustomerRole and op.kind = OpGetApp and op.target = a and a.customer != c and op.outcome = OutAllow }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the no-leak fact lets a non-owned-read be denied with OutDeny (revealing existence) rather than OutNotFound. The injection forces this leaky outcome. F_OwnershipForCustomerRead does not block it because outcome != OutAllow.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoInformationLeakage { some op: Operation, c: User, a: LoanApplication | op.invoker = c and c.role = CustomerRole and op.kind = OpGetApp and op.target = a and a.customer != c and op.outcome = OutDeny }
